title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token unit cost for common production workloads by shipping autotuned defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, a set of quantization profiles per model family, and a first-pass unit-economics CLI for engineering teams to estimate cost impact. This PR bundles three coordinated changes so users get consistent defaults and observability across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.

Summary of changes: 1) Runtime: new autotune module that selects batching window and cache lifetimes by percentile of observed sequence-length and concurrency. 2) Cache defaults: conservative default TTLs and smart prefix-selection heuristics to avoid cache pollution. 3) Quant profiles: JSON profiles per model-family (gpt-like, llama-like) with validated accuracy-to-cost tradeoffs for int8/int4 kernels. 4) Unit-econ tooling: a CLI under tools/unit-econ that consumes call traces and provides per-route token-cost estimates and suggested config diffs. 5) Console: UX to expose recommended defaults and a rollout toggle for opt-in.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime autotune algorithm implemented and validated on perf-canary traces
- [x] Cache heuristics and defaults added
- [x] Quantization profiles generated from offline evals (see profiles/*)
- [x] Unit-econ CLI and CSV importer
- [x] Console integration + docs updates
- [x] End-to-end CI and integration test updates

Backward compatibility and migration: Changes are opt-in by default for Dedicated/Private. Hosted users are rolled out with a canary (5%) and metric guards for latency/quality regressions. Quant profiles are additive; no in-place destructive model conversions are performed by default.

Related: Linear ENG-4512, ENG-4639. See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4512/autotune-batching-and-cache-defaults and internal benchmark results (link in sibling comments).

release_notes: Introduce autotuned defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching with model-family quantization profiles and a new unit-economics CLI. Improves per-token costs by up to 20% on avg for workloads with predictable prefix reuse and medium-length sequences. Rollout: canary 5% hosted, opt-in for Dedicated/Private except when admins enable automatic tuning.
notes_for_operators: Operators: monitor cost-savings and latency SLOs when enabling autotune. Key metrics: per-request token cost, 99th percentile latency, cache hit ratio by route. Feature flag: FEATURE_COST_OPT_AUTOTUNE. Helm values available under helm/redwood/values.cost-optimization.yaml.
